findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the site default locale that now drives fallbacks
findings.body: The LRU cache key is built from the key, `config.locale` and the backend object_id only. With this PR, the result of `translate` also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, because `FallbackLocaleList#[]` inserts that locale into the fallback chain. After the site default locale changes, cached entries for user locales that fell back to the old default (or to :en) keep being served until they are evicted or `reload!` runs. The key should include the fallback chain or the default locale.

findings.title: Fallback chain is rebuilt and reads SiteSetting on every lookup and every request
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` allocates a new array and calls `SiteSetting.default_locale` on each call. `set_locale` in ApplicationController calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` on every request, which invokes `self[I18n.locale]` and so repeats that work. The Fallbacks backend also calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every missing-key translation. This is small per call but runs on the hot path.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! only loads the chain for the current locale, not for an explicitly passed locale
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` loads only `self[I18n.locale]`. Lookups made with an explicit `locale:` argument, or from background jobs that switch locale without going through `set_locale`, will use a fallback chain whose translation files may not be loaded yet. The lazy `load_locale` in the accelerator only covers `config.locale`, so the fallback locales can be missing without any error.

findings.title: Pull request description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR description reads only 'Test 9'. It gives no explanation of why fallbacks move from environment configs into an initializer, why `pluralization.rb` is merged into `i18n.rb`, or how the fallback chain is meant to behave. Reviewers cannot check the intent of the change from the PR itself.
